packageRules.description: Group all GitHub Actions updates into a single PR

Keep internal trufflesecurity actions and reusable workflows on their floating ref instead of SHA-pinning them. Internal actions are org-controlled, so the supply-chain risk is internal; pinning them only adds Renovate noise on every internal release. Scoped by regex because Renovate names a reusable-workflow dependency after its repo (e.g. 'trufflesecurity/.github'), and the leading dot defeats glob '*' matching (see trufflesecurity/slack-integration-service#568 / SCAN-914).

Don't apply the release-age cooldown to pins and digest re-pins. These introduce no new upstream release to age (a pin locks an already-allowed version; a digest re-pin/pinDigest is a hardening action), and minimumReleaseAge has no reliable timestamp to evaluate for digests, which leaves renovate/stability-days stuck pending. Real version upgrades (major/minor/patch) keep the 3-day delay; security updates already bypass it via vulnerabilityAlerts.

Don't apply the release-age cooldown to lock file maintenance. A lockfile refresh is carried out by the package manager rather than resolved from one upstream release, so there is no timestamp for minimumReleaseAge to evaluate. Under Renovate's timestamp-required default, a missing timestamp reads as 'not old enough', so renovate/stability-days pins to pending permanently and never clears on a rebase. That silently defeats the lockFileMaintenance automerge configured above, because automerge waits on a check that cannot pass. Kept as its own rule rather than folded into the pin/digest exemption because the rationale differs and is permanent: pins and digests lack a reliable timestamp, whereas lock file maintenance has none by design and always will. Deliberately not scoped by datasource, unlike Renovate's npm-only security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm preset, because this preset applies minimumReleaseAge to every ecosystem and none of them carry a lock-file-maintenance timestamp.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ Renovate did not validate release age for the packages in this PR. Lock file maintenance hands resolution to the package manager, and neither Yarn nor Go runs a release-age check of its own, so a freshly published version can land here with no cooldown. CI and whatever supply-chain scanning this repo runs are the only gates.

ℹ️ This refresh re-resolves every dependency within the ranges already declared in the manifests. Where a range is loose (a caret on an npm direct dependency), a direct dependency can move a minor version in this PR without ever appearing as a version upgrade.
